title: The opening of the chest
hook: Muslim reports that as a boy his chest was opened by angels and his heart washed

segments.voice: Yesterday, barakah, the blessing that came with the baby nobody wanted. Your line was: blessing came with him.

Boys are playing in the open country of the Banu Sa'd. Suddenly they scatter and run, shouting to the boy's foster mother: Muhammad has been killed! The family rushes out and finds him alive, his face pale. Something has happened to him that the other children saw only from a distance. Sahih Muslim keeps the account, from Anas ibn Malik, a companion of the Prophet ﷺ. Today: sharh as-sadr.
screen: `BOYS AT PLAY.` → `"MUHAMMAD HAS BEEN KILLED!"` → `ALIVE, AND PALE.`

segments.voice: Here is what Muslim reports. While the boy was playing, Jibril came to him, laid him down, and opened his chest. He took out the heart, drew out a clot from it, and said: this was the share of Satan in you. Then he washed the heart in a basin of gold, with the water of Zamzam, and put it back in its place. Anas adds a small detail that brings the whole thing close: he says he used to see the mark of the stitching on the Prophet's chest. Ibn Ishaq tells the same event in Halimah's voice, with two men in white, and says it frightened the family into taking the boy back to his mother in Mecca. So the sources differ on the details, and say so. What does the story mean? Readers take it in different ways. Some take it as a real event that happened to his body. Others stress what it points to: a heart prepared early, cleaned of what pulls toward harm, before anything was asked of it. Some commentators connect it with the opening of surah ninety-four, which Pickthall translates: "Have We not caused thy bosom to dilate." The Arabic there speaks of opening, or expanding, the chest. Notice what the story does not say. It doesn't say the boy did anything to earn it. He was playing. The washing came to him, the way water comes to a dry field. And notice the water: Zamzam, the well his grandfather found again, the water of Hajar's search.
screen: `JIBRIL OPENS THE CHEST.` · `WASHED WITH ZAMZAM IN A GOLD BASIN.` · `ANAS SAW THE STITCHING MARK.` · `A HEART PREPARED EARLY.` · then, large: `HAVE WE NOT CAUSED THY BOSOM TO DILATE.`

segments.voice: If there's water near you, wash your hands and face slowly; if not, do it in your mind, cool water over the wrists and palms, then cupped to your face for one breath, and let one thing you've been carrying go with it. Muslims wash before prayer in a set order; this is not that, just a slow washing. If you pray, you can ask Allah for a clean heart in your own words.
Zamzam, the well his grandfather found again, whose water washed the boy's heart clean in the account of the opening of his chest. Today's word.
Your line: a washed heart. Tomorrow, Aminah at Abwa. See you there.

howItsDone: Muslims know this event as sharh al-sadr, the opening of the chest; it is retold in sirah and hadith study, and some connect it with the opening of surah al-Sharh (94).
